history.dynasty: Satavahana (attributed - built by Satakarni II per local tradition, claimed as originally a Jain mandiram); converted/reconsecrated as a Shiva temple under the Kakatiyas
history.period: Claimed ~500 years old by local sources - but this is chronologically inconsistent with the Satavahana attribution (Satakarni II ~1st century BCE) - verify
history.summary: The 'Neela Kanteshwara Temple [Nizamabad]' is the well-known Sri Neelakanteshwara (Kanteshwar) Temple in Kanteshwar colony, Nizamabad town - about 2.2 km from Nizamabad bus station on the Hyderabad-Nagpur highway. CSV town is correct. Identity certainty: HIGH - this is the famous Shiva temple of Nizamabad. The deity is a Swayambhu linga named Neelakanteshwara for Shiva's blue throat. The complex is notable for a Trimurti presence (Shiva in Swayambhu form, Vishnu reclining as Padmanabhaswamy, Brahma on his lotus). Architecture is Nagara style with Chalukyan elements on the gopuram and Kakatiya floral work, inside a fortress-like wall with stone pillars, a monolithic Nandi, a Dakshinamukhi Anjaneya and an ancient well; one review notes the main linga plus two adjacent Shivalingams and three more in the temple pond. HISTORY CONFLICT: local sources claim the temple was built by Satavahana king Satakarni II for the Jains and converted to a Shiva temple in the Kakatiya period, while also dating it to 'about 500 years ago' - inconsistent with a Satavahana date. The grand annual festival is Rathasaptami with a chariot ceremony; sun rays fall on the lingam only on that day.
